# ui::BringIntoViewOptions

Header: `winui/ui/Element.hpp`.

Where in the viewport a scrolling ancestor puts the element [Element::start_bring_into_view()](element.md#start_bring_into_view) reveals. With no ratio on an axis the ancestor scrolls as little as it can (the element's near edge, or its far edge when it sticks out past the far side). A ratio places the same point of the element and of the viewport together: 0 the near edges, 0.5 the centers, 1 the far edges. The offsets are added to where that lands.

Example: 
```cpp
// Center the row vertically in its Scroll, animated.
auto row = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Row 42");
row->start_bring_into_view({.vertical_alignment_ratio = 0.5f, .animation_desired = true});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `horizontal_alignment_ratio` | `OptionalFloat` |  | Where across the viewport's width the element lands, 0..1; unset scrolls as little as it can. |
| `vertical_alignment_ratio` | `OptionalFloat` |  | Where down the viewport's height the element lands, 0..1; unset scrolls as little as it can. |
| `horizontal_offset` | `float` | `0.0f` | DIPs added to the horizontal position the ratio (or the smallest scroll) gives. |
| `vertical_offset` | `float` | `0.0f` | DIPs added to the vertical position the ratio (or the smallest scroll) gives. |
| `animation_desired` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the scroll animates (a [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll)'s scroll_to()) or jumps. |
| `target_rect` | `std::optional<Rect>` |  | The part of the element to reveal, relative to its own top-left; the whole element when unset. |
